entries.defect: The op-only walker (gen_repeat_body) emitted every greedy/non-greedy Optional as a plain one-token first-set check, so it ignored the lowered strategy (lookahead, scan guard, shape lookahead, `??` ATN). Optionals inside LR-suffix bodies were therefore mis-decided.

findings.summary: A required group inside a repeat whose alternatives share a first token no longer reports an error when no alternative matches, so an invalid input parses as clean.
findings.detail: `gen_consume_group_store_op` and `gen_general_group_store_op` no longer emit the old check after the overlap dispatch: `if let None = opt { p.fail(...)? }`, which became unreachable once the accumulator went away. The dispatch built by `gen_simplecst_overlap_loop` / `gen_general_overlap_loop` is an `if grp_kind in FIRST(...) {...}` chain with no `else`. So when the current token matches no alternative, the group takes no branch, records nothing and adds no diagnostic. For `+` repeats the first iteration runs without a guard. Reproduced with `r : (a | b)+ EOF ; a : X Y ; b : X Z ;` (a and b share first token X): `parse("")` returns `ok() == true` with tree `(r)`, though `+` requires at least one a or b. Before this change the generated parser returned Err ("expected A").

findings.summary: A rule that matches no tokens now gets a node whose span is reversed (end < start), because the rule wrapper closes nodes with an unclamped `p.last_end()`.
findings.detail: `gen_rule_entry_wrapper` opens each node at `p.peek_start()` and closes it with `p.b.finish_node(p.last_end())`. `tree_build_node` builds `Span::new(start, end)` from those values as-is. When a rule (or the whole input) matches nothing, `last_end()` is the end of the previous token, or 0 at the start of input, which is before `peek_start()`. The old emitter clamped this case on purpose with `Span::new(start, i32::max(start, p.last_end()))`, and the removed `gen_clamped_span_field` documented why. Reproduced with `opt_sep_list.g4`: `parse("   ")` returns `ok()` but `root.span` is `3..0`. Anything that uses spans (LSP, highlighting ranges, `Span::len`) gets negative lengths.

findings.summary: A mandatory `(a | b)+` repetition whose alternatives share a first token now matches zero iterations without any diagnostic, so input that is missing the required element parses cleanly.

If the next token is in none of the alternatives' first sets, no `if/else if` arm fires, nothing is consumed, and no error is raised. entries.defect: walk_and_delete propagated NotFound errors from read_dir, the directory entries, file_type and remove_file, so a file or directory removed concurrently during output reconcile aborted the whole pipeline with an I/O error.

findings.summary: Output paths with `.` segments (e.g. `./lib.wado`) are recorded un-normalized, so `reconcile_outputs` deletes the file the generator just wrote.
findings.detail: `validate_rel_output_path` accepts `Component::CurDir`, and `execute` builds the recorded path as `InvocationPath::normalize("{output_dir}/{rel}")`. `normalize` only strips a leading `./`, so the kept path becomes `build/kiln/g/./lib.wado`. `walk_and_delete` compares against the real on-disk path `build/kiln/g/lib.wado`, finds no match, sees the `#![generated]` marker and deletes the fresh output. The lockfile still lists it, so every later run is a cache miss that again generates and deletes the file. Reproduced with a generator returning `./lib.wado`: after `run_pipeline` the outcome had deleted=["build/kiln/g/lib.wado"] and the file was gone.

findings.summary: When one invocation's output dir contains another's, reconciling the outer dir deletes the inner invocation's freshly generated files.
findings.detail: `run_pipeline` keeps a separate kept-list for each output dir, but `reconcile_outputs` walks each dir recursively and only checks that dir's own list. With `output-dir = "gen"` for one invocation and `"gen/inner"` for another, reconciling `gen` deletes `gen/inner/b.wado` because it is not in the outer list. The same happens with `output-dir = "."`, which normalizes to the project root and wipes every other generator's outputs. Reproduced: the outcome had deleted=["gen/inner/b.wado"] and the file was missing while the lockfile still recorded it.

findings.summary: `cache_matches` ignores the generator identity, so changing `module = "ns:proto@1.0.0"` to `@1.1.0` still counts as a cache hit and the new generator never runs.
findings.detail: `run_pipeline` only compares `options_hash`, and `cache_matches` only compares primary, inputs, reads and outputs. Neither checks `entry.generator` against `generator_identity(&invocation.module)`, and `compose_cache_key`, which does include the identity, is never used. After a generator version bump, stale outputs from the old generator are reused and the lockfile keeps `generator = "ns:proto@1.0.0"`. Reproduced: on the second run with the 1.1.0 manifest the outcome was cached=["g"] with 0 generator runs.

findings.summary: The host `read-file` import lets a sandboxed generator read any file on the host (absolute paths or `..`), not just files in the project.
findings.detail: `KilnHostState::read_file` passes the path the generator chose straight to `FilesystemCompilerHost::load_source`, which does `base_path.join(path)`. A path such as `/etc/passwd` or `../../.ssh/id_rsa` escapes the project, so a third-party build-dependency generator can read secrets and embed them in generated output. That breaks the isolation the module docs promise ("only the two host imports… determinism guarantee"). Not reproduced: it needs a compiled Wasm generator component, which I could not build within this review. The code path is direct, though: `wado_lsp::FilesystemCompilerHost::load_source` is a bare `std::fs::read(base_path.join(path))`.

findings.summary: A cached result is reused after the generator module changes, because the cache check never compares the recorded `generator` identity.
findings.detail: `run_pipeline` finds a prior entry by invocation name and `options_hash` only. `cache_matches` then checks the primary file, the inputs, the reads and the outputs, but never compares `entry.generator` with `generator_identity(&invocation.module)`. If a user changes `module = "ns:proto@1.0.0"` to `@2.0.0` and leaves the schema alone, the build reports the invocation as cached and keeps the output from the old generator. The lockfile also keeps saying the old generator made it. Reproduced: running again with the module changed to 2.0.0 gave `cached: ["g"], executed: []`.

findings.summary: After `output-dir` changes, the cache still hits, so nothing is written to the new directory.
findings.detail: `cache_matches` re-hashes the output paths recorded in the lockfile (still under the old directory). It never checks that they sit under the invocation's current `output_dir`. When the user changes `output-dir`, the old files still match, so the invocation counts as cached. The new directory stays empty, and code that imports from it breaks. The prior entry is written back unchanged, so the lockfile keeps pointing at the old directory. Reproduced: changing `output-dir` to `gen/new` gave `cached: ["g"]` and no `gen/new/a.wado`.

findings.summary: When one invocation's output directory is nested inside another's, cleanup deletes the inner invocation's freshly generated files.
findings.detail: Cleanup runs once per directory and walks it recursively. Each directory's kept list holds only the outputs of invocations whose `output_dir` is exactly that directory. With `output-dir = "gen"` and `output-dir = "gen/inner"`, the walk of `gen` goes into `gen/inner` and deletes the inner generator's output, which is not on `gen`'s kept list. The lockfile still records that file, so every build regenerates it and deletes it again. Reproduced: `deleted: ["gen/inner/b.wado"]` right after it was generated.

findings.summary: Generators get file reads that are not limited to the project: `read-file("../x")` or an absolute path reads any file on the machine.
findings.detail: `run_generator` hands the plain `wado_lsp::FilesystemCompilerHost` to the kiln runtime. `read_file` passes the path straight to `load_source`, which just does `base_path.join(path)`. Absolute paths and `..` segments therefore reach any file the user can read. A third-party generator from a registry can read secrets such as `~/.ssh` keys or `.env` files and copy them into its generated output. Reproduced: `load_source("../secret.txt")` from the project root returned the file's contents.

findings.summary: On the real CLI host, a missing file reaches the generator as `io(...)` instead of `not-found`.
findings.detail: `read_file` returns `HostError::NotFound` only for `SourceError::NotFound`. The CLI's filesystem host never produces that variant: every failure, including a missing file, comes back as `SourceError::IoError`. Generators therefore cannot tell an optional include that is absent from a real I/O failure, and treat an absent file as a hard error. Reproduced: loading a missing file returned `Err(IoError { ..., "No such file or directory" })`.

findings.summary: If a generator reads a file by absolute path, its cache never hits again.
findings.detail: `build_cache_entry` and `cache_matches` pass read paths through `InvocationPath::normalize`, which drops empty path segments and so removes the leading `/`. `/abs/x.proto` is stored as `abs/x.proto`. The next build loads that relative path, the load fails, and the generator re-runs on every build. Reproduced: the lockfile recorded `path = "abs/x.proto"` and the second run executed again instead of hitting the cache.
